item.title: Curry Barker's New Short Is Out and It Could Be the Obsession Sequel We Need
item.description: All eyes have been on director Curry Barker since the release of his indie horror movie , Obsession . It not only had an astonishing box office run, but it was also critically acclaimed, with a 93% rating on Rotten Tomatoes . Barker's ideas are one-of-a-kind, which is why fans were excited to learn that Mama Bear , a new short film, would be coming their way right before Halloween .

item.title: The Witcher Meets Carrie in a New Epic Fantasy Book
item.description: Andrzej Sapkowski drew on Slavic mythology when writing The Witcher , his legendary fantasy series about a war torn world filled with magic and monsters. If you’ve been playing through The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt – Remastered and are looking for some of the same dark fairy tale flavor, you’ll want to check out a new fantasy epic kicking off in November.

item.title: Phantom Blade Zero Director Reveals How He Made 'A Playable Kung Fu Movie’ with Donnie Yen
item.description: Director Soulframe Liang said he wanted to “create a playable kung fu movie” with Phantom Blade Zero . As part of a preview event hosted by S-Game in China last month, Polygon spoke with him in a group Q&A and a one-on-one chat. That preview event also included a visit to the developer’s Shanghai motion capture studio, where the press heard from combat director Yang Liu.

item.title: My Chemical Romance and Lauren Tsai Team Up for Short Movie Featuring Hideo Kojima
item.description: Artist Lauren Tsai, creator of the stop-motion series The Dying World, has collaborated with New Jersey band My Chemical Romance. Drawing on The Dying World and its characters, she created a short film based on "The End," the first song on My Chemical Romance's 2006 album The Black Parade .

item.title: Forget 'Carrie,' Mike Flanagan's Next Movie Could Fix A Misunderstood Cult Classic
item.description: My relationship to horror started like a lot of people’s: I was a ridiculously scared child. The thought of Freddy Krueger’s claws was enough to drive me to tears. But then, I grew up, and I became obsessed with the genre and its controlled fears. I have a soft spot for exorcism storylines, featuring the kind of horror that lingers and makes its way into your home. Blame it on my Catholic upbringing, but few things are more disturbing to me than watching Regan MacNeil (Linda Blair) spider walk down the stairs.

item.title: 10 Queer Fairy Tale Retellings Better Than the Originals
item.description: As a queer woman growing up, it was pretty easy to neg on all things fairy-tale. Perhaps I had reason to, as mockery of all things Disney has grown popular in recent years.

item.title: Hideo Kojima's Death Stranding Anime Looks Impressive in First Official Trailer
item.description: Hideo Kojima's Death Stranding series brought the Metal Gear Solid creator's trademark arthouse approach to video games to full fruition. With no plans for Death Stranding 3 , besides a concept draft, fans are instead looking forward to the game's universe expanding into different media, including anime.

item.title: 5 Classic JRPGs with Virtually Perfect Battle Systems
item.description: Many role-playing games have a familiar, turn-based combat system. Your options are usually riffs on one of four actions: attack, defend, use magic, or use an item. Even with that very basic template, you’re usually in for a pretty fun time saving the world with a group of pals. But if it’s not snappy and satisfying, or if battles drag on too long, you’re probably bouncing off that game.

item.title: 34 Years Later, Hobbes' Wisest 'Calvin and Hobbes' Line Is Still a Perfect Comic Strip Quote
item.description: Here's something that might win you some points in a trivia game someday: Bill Watterson named the protagonists of Calvin and Hobbes after two European philosophers. John Calvin (1509-1564) was a controversial theologian whose ideas gave rise to the predestination-oriented Calvinist branch of Protestantism (thus mucking everything up for everyone for centuries to come). Thomas Hobbes (1588-1679) wrote Leviathan , one of the foundational works of social contract theory.

item.title: 10 Essential Fantasy Books You Need to Read at Least Once in Your Life
item.description: Fantasy has always offered a way to step beyond the boundaries of reality, inviting readers into worlds where the impossible becomes part of everyday life. The genre stretches back to ancient folklore, epic poetry, and fairy tales, existing long before the modern fantasy novel took shape, in which sorcery and magical worlds abound. From the mythological journeys of Homer to the dreamlike stories of George MacDonald, imaginative literature has continually found new ways to explore humanity through the extraordinary.
